name: Ile

attributes.attribute: a Scottish goddess for whom the isle of Islay was named
described at times as a queen or princess called Yula of Denmark
an island in the Hebrides, the first inauguration site for the Lords of the Isles

sources: Straffon, Cheryl. *The Earth Goddess: Celtic and Pagan Legacy of the Landscape*. London: Blandford, 1997, 147.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Ile is a Scottish goddess. She is also called Eila or Yula. One of the largest of the Hebrides is the isle of Islay. It was named for this goddess. Sometimes she is described as a queen or princess. She is then called Yula of Denmark. Ile is an obscure figure. Yet the island that bears her name is better known. It was the first site for the Lords of the Isles. Their ruler stepped on a stone carved with footprints to receive the office.
objective: Document the Scottish goddess Ile and the island Islay named for her.
key_results: Record the names Eila and Yula.
Record Islay as named for Ile.
Note the inauguration rite of the Lords of the Isles.
